papers.title: eFAIR: Fair LLM Serving under Hourly Electricity Commitments
papers.abstract: Datacenters can procure electricity in day-ahead markets by committing to energy purchases for individual hours. For LLM services operating within these hourly budgets, maximizing aggregate throughput alone may still leave individual requests waiting or receiving much slower service than desired. papers.title: LEDGE: An Efficient Simulator for Distributed LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Devices
papers.abstract: Evaluating distributed large language model (LLM) serving on heterogeneous edge devices requires exploring diverse model partitions, device placements, and network conditions, making repeated physical experiments costly. An efficient simulator for edge LLM serving must support diverse, fine-grained placement configurations, capture runtime behavior, and accurately predict execution times while keeping simulation overhead low. We present LEDGE, a lightweight simulator for fast, fine-grained evaluation of distributed LLM serving on heterogeneous edge devices without executing tensor operations.

papers.title: A Hardware-Aware Comprehensive Study of Edge Vision Deployment with A Unified Hardware-Model-Runtime Mapping Framework
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of deep learning has driven the deployment of computer vision directly on resource-constrained edge devices. However, the extreme heterogeneity of edge hardware architectures poses major challenges in selecting and designing suitable vision models. This survey bridges the gap between edge hardware constraints, model architectures, and deployment software toolchains. We establish a comprehensive taxonomy classifying edge hardware into three distinct tiers: mid-range devices (GPUs and dedicated NPUs or TPUs), dedicated embedded MPU or SoC processors, and microcontrollers (MCUs).

papers.title: Jetriever: Shifting Agent Memory Retrieval from Similarity to Utility

papers.title: From Sensors to Silicon: Causal Cross-Layer Self-Healing Edge AI for Secure and Energy-Adaptive IoT Systems
papers.abstract: The migration of artificial intelligence from centralized cloud infrastructure to resource-constrained Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices reduces communication latency and improves data locality, but it also tightly couples sensing quality, inference behavior, microarchitectural activity, hardware reliability, security, and energy management within the same physical node. papers.problem_zh: 这篇论文解决了安全和能量自适应物联网系统中的边缘AI问题。
papers.method_zh: 提出了一种因果跨层自愈边缘AI框架，能够在资源受限的IoT设备上实现高效的推理和自适应能量管理。
